Market research firm Omdia's latest report has further revealed the product roadmap for Apple's upcoming MacBook Pro, MacBook Air, and iPad models over the next few years. Below are the details of the new devices anticipated in the report.

Omdia's anticipated new MacBook and iPad models are as follows

Omdia has published an extensive report specifically discussing the display panels used in the next-generation MacBook and iPad. Based on the firm's research into display technology, they have released a product roadmap for new devices starting from this autumn and extending all the way to 2029.

Here's an overview of the new devices expected in the report:

Second half of 2026

  • MacBook Pro/Ultra: 14.3-inch and 16.3-inch OLED displays
  • iPad mini: 8.4-inch OLED display, 60Hz refresh rate

First half of 2027

  • MacBook Air: 13.6-inch and 15.4-inch LCD displays
  • iPad Air: 11-inch and 13-inch OLED displays, 60Hz refresh rate

Mid 2027

  • iPad Pro: 11-inch and 13-inch OLED displays, incorporating COE technology

Second half of 2027

  • MacBook Pro/Ultra: 14.3-inch and 16.3-inch OLED displays, incorporating LTPO technology

First half of 2028

2029

  • MacBook: 13.6-inch OLED display, equipped with LTPO and COE technology

Key highlights from the MacBook and iPad report worth noting

There are several noteworthy details in the report. For example, the report states that after the OLED version of the MacBook Pro/Ultra launches this autumn, the mini-LED version of the MacBook Pro will continue to be sold until at least 2028. This could support the idea that the "Ultra" brand name will be used exclusively for the OLED version.

Second, the 13.6-inch MacBook slated for 2029 has been singled out in Omdia's timeline as a separate new model. However, based on previous rumours, this device is very likely just the OLED version of the MacBook Air that Bloomberg and Ming-Chi Kuo had previously reported on.

The MacBook Neo is conspicuously absent from this roadmap, but this makes perfect sense—as an entry-level product, it's not expected to see any display upgrades in the short term; this also explains why the basic iPad wasn't mentioned.

Finally, Omdia predicts that the OLED version of the MacBook Pro/MacBook Ultra will offer an M5 Ultra chip option. However, this claim appears to be more of a speculation rather than a definitive report.

What are your thoughts on this Mac and iPad product roadmap? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
